newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas mostly higher amid cold weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas mostly higher amid cold weather.

text.p: U.S spot natgas prices were mostly higher Monday, propped up by continued cold weather across most of the U.S. and weather-related power outages in Texas, market sources said.

Gulf Coast prices gained about 10 cents to the $3.90-4.00 per mmBtu range as ice storms in Houston caused extensive power outages and cold temperatures lingered throughout the eastern two-thirds of the U.S.
Similar prices were evident in south Texas where Houston Light and Power said 180,000 electricity customers were without service due to ice-ladened power lines.
Further east, New York city-gate prices gained as much as 50 cents to about $5.00, lifted by cold temperatures in the area and forecasts for the arrival of another cold front Thursday.
Despite the stronger Gulf and Northeast prices, values in the Midcontinent fell by an average of 50 cents to the $4.30-4.35 range, still about 10 cents over January indices.
Temperatures are expected to moderate Tuesday and Wednesday in the Midwest but still remain below normal. Another cold front is expected to land late this week.
Helping to relieve the Chicago market was Northern Illinois Gas' announcement that it lifted its Critical Day period for Tuesday deliveries after three days of limiting storage withdrawals.
Also, Natural Gas Pipeline said its critical time was no longer in effect.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices were up by about 15 cents to the $4.20-4.25 range, with deals reported done anywhere from $4.05 early to $4.40 late.
At the southern California border, prices jumped to about $4.30, up 50 cents from Friday, as below-normal temperatures moved into the Southwest and northern California.
